description: Verifies that an AWS Systems Manager Distributor package reached one Google Cloud virtual machine, by reading the Google Cloud OS policy compliance report for the OS policy that AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp assigned. The document authenticates to Google Cloud using a configured Cloud Connector, verifies that the virtual machine is running with VM Manager enabled, reads the current revision of the named OS policy orchestrator's assignment, and then checks the virtual machine's compliance report. If the target virtual machine is not found, for example because it was deleted after AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp listed it, the runbook ends successfully without verifying. Google Cloud VM Manager can take up to 24 hours to apply an OS policy. This runbook is invoked by AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp and is not intended to be run directly.

CloudConnector.description: (Required) The ID of the Systems Manager Cloud Connector that contains your Google Cloud organization, project, and workload identity configuration. This connector provides the credentials needed to authenticate with Google Cloud.

GCPVmResourceId.description: (Required) The relative resource name of the Google Cloud virtual machine to verify the installation on. Format: projects/{project-id}/zones/{zone}/instances/{instance-name}. The optional //compute.googleapis.com/ prefix is accepted. The virtual machine must be in a RUNNING state, must have VM Manager enabled, and its project must be one of the projects this automation is narrowed to. An OS policy compliance report is addressed per virtual machine, so unlike AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp this runbook cannot be run without one.

OSPolicyOrchestratorName.description: (Required) The relative resource name of the Google Cloud OS policy orchestrator whose OS policy assignment this runbook verifies, as AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp reports it in its OrchestratorResourceName output. Format: organizations/{organization-id}/locations/global/policyOrchestrators/{orchestrator-id} or projects/{project-number}/locations/global/policyOrchestrators/{orchestrator-id}. The orchestrator must exist, because the OS policy assignment this runbook reads is the one it names.

OSPolicyAssignmentId.description: (Optional) The PolicyId output of AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp. With OSPolicyDigest and OSPolicyOrchestrationScope, it spares reading the orchestrator, which is read when any of the three is empty.

OSPolicyDigest.description: (Optional) The PolicyDigest output of AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp, a digest of the OS policies the orchestrator writes.

OSPolicyOrchestrationScope.description: (Optional) The OrchestrationScope output of AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp, the orchestrator's scope as JSON, or {} for none.

PackageName.description: (Optional) The name of the Systems Manager Distributor package whose installation is verified. Reported as installation-result telemetry and to the package's publisher, and named in the failure messages; the OS policy assignment this runbook reads comes from OSPolicyOrchestratorName, not from this name.

Action.description: (Optional) Whether the package was installed, uninstalled, or updated. Reported as installation-result telemetry and to the package's publisher; the verification itself is the same for all three. Defaults to Install.

Version.description: (Optional) The version of the package whose installation is verified, as AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp resolved it. Reported as installation-result telemetry and to the package's publisher. If unspecified, the version is reported as unknown.

AutomationAssumeRole.description: (Required) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the IAM role that allows Systems Manager Automation to perform actions on your behalf. This role must allow ssm:GetCloudConnector, ssm:PutConfigurePackageResult, sts:AssumeRole on the Cloud Connector's IAM role, and iam:ListRoleTags on itself; sts:GetWebIdentityToken is the Cloud Connector role's permission, not this one's. It does not need ssm:GetDocument, because this runbook reads the installation result from Google Cloud rather than reading the Distributor package.

mainSteps.name: CheckCompliance
mainSteps.description: Reads the Google Cloud configuration from the Cloud Connector and exchanges the AWS credentials for a Google Cloud access token once. With it, the step verifies the target virtual machine, reads its zone's current revision of the orchestrator's OS policy assignment, and reads and classifies its compliance report once, before waiting. The virtual machine is verified first, because Google Cloud answers a compliance report for a virtual machine that does not exist with the same not-found response as one that has not reported yet: the OS Config API must be enabled for its project, and it must be running with VM Manager enabled. A virtual machine that is not found ends the automation at EvaluateVmExists. The zone's revision says whether it carries the orchestrator's OS policies, which it does not where the last rollout failed; the assignment, OS policies and scope come from the parameters the parent passes, or from the orchestrator when any is empty. An OS Config read refused for a spent per-minute read quota is sent again after waiting a minute or more for it to refill, for up to 450 seconds of waiting across the step's reads. A result, a virtual machine the OS policy does not target, and a failure end the automation without waiting. Otherwise the ReportsParent and ReportSelector outputs are what WaitForCompliance watches: the virtual machine's reports, and the one for this OS policy assignment at a revision a result can count for.

inputs.Script:
import json

from ssm_gcp.providers import DependencyManager
boto3_version, botocore_version, google_auth_version = DependencyManager.setup()
from ssm_gcp.utils.exception_mapper import step_handler
from ssm_gcp.exceptions import ValidationException
from ssm_gcp.providers import (
    OSCONFIG_SERVICE,
    assert_instance_is_running,
    assert_service_enabled,
    assert_zone_shaped,
    check_vm_manager_enabled,
    credential_source,
    first_check_quota_deadline,
    get_assignment_revision,
    get_instance,
    get_orchestrator,
    orchestrated_policy_digest,
    parse_vm_resource_id,
    resolve_cloud_connector_config,
    resolve_gcp_credentials,
    scope_excludes,
    validate_project_in_scope
)
from gcp_verify.report.check import check_report

DOCUMENT_NAME = 'AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp-VerifyInstallation'

_UNCHECKED_OUTPUTS = (
    "assignment_id",
    "assignment_exists",
    "revision_id",
    "revision_create_time",
    "rollout_state",
    "assignment_current",
    "instance_filter",
    "orchestration_scope",
    "verdict",
    "enforcement_log",
    "agent_log",
    "platform",
    "last_run_id",
    "report_revision_id",
    "report_update_time",
    "checked_at",
    "reports_parent",
    "report_selector"
)

@step_handler
def check_compliance(events, context):
    """Verify the target machine, read its zone's assignment, and classify its report once.
    """
    ssm_region = context.get('global:REGION')
    if not ssm_region:
        raise ValueError("Could not determine the AWS Region for this automation execution.")

    quota_deadline = first_check_quota_deadline()

    cloud_connector_id = events.get("cloud_connector_id")
    resource_id = events.get("resource_id")
    automation_assume_role_arn = events.get("automation_assume_role_arn")
    orchestrator_name = events.get("orchestrator_name")

    if not cloud_connector_id:
        raise ValueError("The CloudConnector parameter is required but was not provided.")
    if not resource_id:
        raise ValueError("The GCPVmResourceId parameter is required but was not provided.")
    if not orchestrator_name:
        raise ValueError("The OSPolicyOrchestratorName parameter is required but was not provided.")

    target = parse_vm_resource_id(resource_id)
    project_id = target["project_id"]
    instance_name = target["instance_name"]
    zone = assert_zone_shaped(target["zone"])

    orchestrated = _passed_assignment(
        events.get("assignment_id"),
        events.get("policy_digest"),
        events.get("orchestration_scope")
    )

    config = resolve_cloud_connector_config(
        cloud_connector_id=cloud_connector_id,
        ssm_region=ssm_region
    )
    validate_project_in_scope(config, project_id)

    credentials = resolve_gcp_credentials(
        config,
        automation_assume_role_arn=automation_assume_role_arn,
        role_session_name=DOCUMENT_NAME
    )

    osconfig_api_state = assert_service_enabled(
        project_id, OSCONFIG_SERVICE, credentials
    )

    instance = get_instance(
        project_id,
        zone,
        instance_name,
        credentials,
        tolerate_status=(404,)
    )

    if instance is None:
        return _handle_vm_not_running(
            project_id,
            zone,
            instance_name,
            config["service_account_email"],
            osconfig_api_state
        )

    vm_status = assert_instance_is_running(instance)
    vm_manager_source = check_vm_manager_enabled(
        instance, project_id, credentials
    )
    last_start_timestamp = str(
        getattr(instance, "last_start_timestamp", "") or ""
    )

    orchestrator_read = orchestrated is None
    if orchestrator_read:
        orchestrator = get_orchestrator(orchestrator_name, credentials)
        orchestrated = {
            "assignment_id": _orchestrated_assignment_id(orchestrator),
            "policy_digest": orchestrated_policy_digest(orchestrator),
            "scope": orchestrator.get("orchestrationScope")
        }
    assignment_id = orchestrated["assignment_id"]
    payload_digest = orchestrated["policy_digest"]
    scope = orchestrated["scope"]

    revision = get_assignment_revision(
        project_id, zone, assignment_id, credentials,
        quota_deadline=quota_deadline
    )

    assignment_current = str(
        not payload_digest
        or not revision["policy_digest"]
        or revision["policy_digest"] == payload_digest
        or scope_excludes(scope, project_id, zone, credentials)
    ).lower()
    assignment_exists = str(revision["exists"]).lower()
    instance_filter = json.dumps(revision["instance_filter"], sort_keys=True)
    orchestration_scope = json.dumps(
        scope if isinstance(scope, dict) else {}, sort_keys=True
    )

    report = check_report(
        {
            "project_id": project_id,
            "zone": zone,
            "instance_name": instance_name,
            "last_start_timestamp": last_start_timestamp,
            "assignment_id": assignment_id,
            "revision_id": revision["revision_id"],
            "revision_create_time": revision["revision_create_time"],
            "assignment_exists": assignment_exists,
            "rollout_state": revision["rollout_state"],
            "assignment_current": assignment_current,
            "instance_filter": instance_filter,
            "orchestration_scope": orchestration_scope,
            "package_name": events.get("package_name"),
            "package_version": events.get("package_version"),
            "action": events.get("action")
        },
        credentials,
        final_check=False,
        quota_deadline=quota_deadline
    )

    aws_log = {
      "boto3_version": boto3_version,
      "botocore_version": botocore_version,
      "google_auth_version": google_auth_version,
      "credential_source": credential_source(),
      "vm_found": "true",
      "vm_status": vm_status,
      "osconfig_api_state": osconfig_api_state,
      "vm_manager_source": vm_manager_source,
      "orchestrator_read": str(orchestrator_read).lower(),
      "assignment_exists": assignment_exists,
      "revision_id": revision["revision_id"],
      "baseline": str(revision["baseline"]).lower(),
      "reconciling": str(revision["reconciling"]).lower(),
      "assignment_current": assignment_current,
      "instance_filter_os_count": str(
          len(revision["instance_filter"].get("inventories") or ())
      )
    }
    aws_log.update(report["aws_log"])

    return {
        "project_id": project_id,
        "zone": zone,
        "instance_name": instance_name,
        "service_account_email": config["service_account_email"],
        "vm_found": True,
        "vm_status": vm_status,
        "last_start_timestamp": last_start_timestamp,
        "assignment_id": assignment_id,
        "assignment_exists": assignment_exists,
        "revision_id": revision["revision_id"],
        "revision_create_time": revision["revision_create_time"],
        "rollout_state": revision["rollout_state"],
        "assignment_current": assignment_current,
        "instance_filter": instance_filter,
        "orchestration_scope": orchestration_scope,
        "verdict": report["verdict"],
        "compliance_detail": report["compliance_detail"],
        "enforcement_log": report["enforcement_log"],
        "agent_log": report["agent_log"],
        "platform": report["platform"],
        "last_run_id": report["last_run_id"],
        "report_revision_id": report["report_revision_id"],
        "report_update_time": report["report_update_time"],
        "checked_at": report["checked_at"],
        "reports_parent": report["reports_parent"],
        "report_selector": report["report_selector"],
        "aws_log": aws_log
    }

def _handle_vm_not_running(
    project_id, zone, instance_name, service_account_email, osconfig_api_state
):
    """Given a machine Compute Engine does not have, returns the payload EvaluateVmExists ends on.
    """
    payload = dict.fromkeys(_UNCHECKED_OUTPUTS, "")
    payload.update(
        project_id=project_id,
        zone=zone,
        instance_name=instance_name,
        service_account_email=service_account_email,
        vm_found=False,
        vm_status="",
        last_start_timestamp="",
        compliance_detail={"compliance_state": "", "reason": ""},
        aws_log={
            "boto3_version": boto3_version,
            "botocore_version": botocore_version,
            "google_auth_version": google_auth_version,
            "credential_source": credential_source(),
            "vm_found": "false",
            "zone": zone,
            "osconfig_api_state": osconfig_api_state,
            "message": "Target VM not found, skipping verification"
        }
    )
    return payload

def _passed_assignment(assignment_id, digest, scope):
    if not (assignment_id and digest and scope):
        return None

    if isinstance(scope, str):
        try:
            scope = json.loads(scope)
        except ValueError:
            scope = None
    if not isinstance(scope, dict):
        raise ValidationException(
            "The OSPolicyOrchestrationScope parameter is not a JSON object. "
            "Pass the OrchestrationScope output of AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp, "
            "or leave it empty to have the orchestrator read."
        )

    return {
        "assignment_id": str(assignment_id),
        "policy_digest": str(digest),
        "scope": scope
    }

def _orchestrated_assignment_id(orchestrator):
    """Given the orchestrator, returns the ID of the assignment it orchestrates.
    """
    if orchestrator is None:
        raise ValidationException(
            "The Google Cloud OS policy orchestrator named by "
            "OSPolicyOrchestratorName does not exist, so no OS policy "
            "assignment will ever be created for this virtual machine. Run "
            "AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp for this "
            "package, then pass its OrchestratorResourceName output to this automation."
        )

    orchestrated = orchestrator.get("orchestratedResource")
    assignment_id = (
        orchestrated.get("id") if isinstance(orchestrated, dict) else None
    )
    if not assignment_id:
        raise ValidationException(
            "The Google Cloud OS policy orchestrator named by "
            "OSPolicyOrchestratorName orchestrates no OS policy assignment. "
            "Pass the OrchestratorResourceName output of "
            "AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp to this "
            "automation."
        )

    return str(assignment_id)

mainSteps.name: EvaluateVmExists
mainSteps.description: Continue to compliance verification when CheckCompliance found the VM. When the VM was not found, e.g., a VM created moments ago that is not yet visible due to eventual consistency, end the runbook successfully.

mainSteps.name: ShouldWaitForCompliance
mainSteps.description: Waits only while Google Cloud is still working, and otherwise goes straight to the final check.

mainSteps.name: WaitForCompliance
mainSteps.description: Watches the target virtual machine's OS policy compliance reports until the one for this OS policy assignment, at a revision a result can count for, says COMPLIANT or NON_COMPLIANT. It lists the reports rather than reading the one, because Google Cloud answers a report not written yet with a not-found error, which would end the wait at once, and an empty list keeps it polling. It waits up to 20 hours, and a read that fails ends it. VM Manager can take up to 24 hours to apply an OS policy, so a virtual machine still waiting then is reported as a timeout, and running the automation again keeps waiting. The step is not critical: running out of time is reported by AssertCompliance from what GetComplianceReport then reads.

mainSteps.name: GetComplianceReport
mainSteps.description: Reads the Google Cloud OS policy compliance report for the target virtual machine once the wait is over, and classifies it for AssertCompliance to report. If CheckCompliance already reached a terminal verdict (COMPLIANT, FAILED, or NOT_TARGETED) before any wait, that verdict is reused as-is rather than read again, to avoid spending a second Google Cloud OS Config read from the virtual machine's per-region, per-minute zonal read quota for no new information. A report still waiting after WaitForCompliance runs out of time is reported as a timeout, while a read that fails here fails the attempt, and is tried up to three times, because there is no later check to wait for. When there is no report, it reads the virtual machine's OS inventory, and when there is no assignment in its zone, the orchestrator's scope, to tell a virtual machine that has not reported yet from one the OS policy will never reach. When the report says the virtual machine is not running, it reads the virtual machine again, because Google Cloud rewrites a report about once an hour and a virtual machine started since then is waited on rather than failed. A report left standing for over two hours on a virtual machine running that long means its OS Config agent stopped reporting, and ends the check as failed. When the installation succeeded or failed, its EnforcementLog output is the end of the virtual machine's log of the run that wrote the report. It is empty when the report records no run, which is the case for a report from a later cycle that found nothing to install. When no OS Config agent ever reported, its AgentLog output is the agent's last lines on the virtual machine's serial console, if the Cloud Connector's service account may read it.

inputs.Script:
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from ssm_gcp.providers import DependencyManager
boto3_version, botocore_version, google_auth_version = DependencyManager.setup()
from ssm_gcp.utils.exception_mapper import step_handler
from ssm_gcp.providers import (
    TERMINAL_VERDICTS,
    credential_source,
    resolve_cloud_connector_config,
    resolve_gcp_credentials
)
from gcp_verify.report.check import check_report, json_mapping

DOCUMENT_NAME = 'AWS-InstallDistributorPackageOnGcp-VerifyInstallation'

@step_handler
def get_compliance_report(events, context):
    """Read one compliance report and say whether it is a result.

    If CheckCompliance already reached a terminal verdict before any
    wait, reuse it: it will not change and no newer report exists, so
    re-reading only spends the GCP OS Config read quota for nothing.
    """
    prior_verdict = str(events.get("prior_verdict") or "")
    if prior_verdict in TERMINAL_VERDICTS:
        return _reuse_prior_verdict(events)

    ssm_region = context.get('global:REGION')
    if not ssm_region:
        raise ValueError("Could not determine the AWS Region for this automation execution.")

    cloud_connector_id = events.get("cloud_connector_id")
    automation_assume_role_arn = events.get("automation_assume_role_arn")
    final_check = str(events.get("final_check") or "").lower() == "true"

    if not cloud_connector_id:
        raise ValueError("The CloudConnector parameter is required but was not provided.")
    if not events.get("assignment_id"):
        raise ValueError("The CheckCompliance step returned no Google Cloud OS policy assignment to check.")

    config = resolve_cloud_connector_config(
        cloud_connector_id=cloud_connector_id,
        ssm_region=ssm_region
    )
    credentials = resolve_gcp_credentials(
        config,
        automation_assume_role_arn=automation_assume_role_arn,
        role_session_name=DOCUMENT_NAME
    )

    report = check_report(
        {
            "project_id": events.get("project_id"),
            "zone": events.get("zone"),
            "instance_name": events.get("instance_name"),
            "last_start_timestamp": events.get("last_start_timestamp"),
            "assignment_id": events.get("assignment_id"),
            "revision_id": events.get("revision_id"),
            "revision_create_time": events.get("revision_create_time"),
            "assignment_exists": events.get("assignment_exists"),
            "rollout_state": events.get("rollout_state"),
            "assignment_current": events.get("assignment_current"),
            "instance_filter": events.get("instance_filter"),
            "orchestration_scope": events.get("orchestration_scope"),
            "package_name": events.get("package_name"),
            "package_version": events.get("package_version"),
            "action": events.get("action")
        },
        credentials,
        final_check=final_check
    )

    aws_log = dict(report["aws_log"])
    aws_log["boto3_version"] = boto3_version
    aws_log["botocore_version"] = botocore_version
    aws_log["google_auth_version"] = google_auth_version
    aws_log["credential_source"] = credential_source()

    return {
        "verdict": report["verdict"],
        "compliance_detail": report["compliance_detail"],
        "enforcement_log": report["enforcement_log"],
        "agent_log": report["agent_log"],
        "platform": report["platform"],
        "last_run_id": report["last_run_id"],
        "report_revision_id": report["report_revision_id"],
        "report_update_time": report["report_update_time"],
        "checked_at": report["checked_at"],
        "reports_parent": report["reports_parent"],
        "report_selector": report["report_selector"],
        "aws_log": aws_log
    }

def _reuse_prior_verdict(events):
    """Return CheckCompliance's own terminal result, without re-reading."""
    return {
        "verdict": str(events.get("prior_verdict") or ""),
        "compliance_detail": json_mapping(events.get("prior_compliance_detail")),
        "enforcement_log": str(events.get("prior_enforcement_log") or ""),
        "agent_log": str(events.get("prior_agent_log") or ""),
        "platform": str(events.get("prior_platform") or ""),
        "last_run_id": str(events.get("prior_last_run_id") or ""),
        "report_revision_id": str(events.get("prior_report_revision_id") or ""),
        "report_update_time": str(events.get("prior_report_update_time") or ""),
        "checked_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "reports_parent": str(events.get("prior_reports_parent") or ""),
        "report_selector": str(events.get("prior_report_selector") or ""),
        "aws_log": json_mapping(events.get("prior_aws_log"))
    }

mainSteps.name: AssertCompliance
mainSteps.description: Reports the verification result, and fails the automation if Google Cloud did not report the installation as complete. Giving up on a virtual machine that is still working and reporting one that failed are different outcomes with different messages: VM Manager can take up to 24 hours to apply an OS policy, so a virtual machine that has not reported yet is usually not a problem, while a non-compliant report is. A virtual machine the OS policy does not target is reported as a success, because the package publishes nothing for its operating system. A failure prints the end of the virtual machine's log of the run, or of its OS Config agent's serial console lines, in this step's output. A failure the OS Config agent retries also says when Google Cloud recorded it, whether that was before this automation first checked, and when the agent's next run, about an hour later, will have reported. A success or failure the report records a run of the package's scripts for is also sent to Systems Manager with ssm:PutConfigurePackageResult, as the SSM Agent does after an installation on EC2, so that it counts in the metrics the package's publisher sees. Sending it is best-effort: an error is recorded in AWSLog and does not change the result.
